reason: E3 directly demonstrates phase-selective recrystallization in a eutectic HEA, achieving ~35% uniform elongation and ~2 GPa true stress, fully supporting the core premises. E1 and E2 confirm the baseline problem of dislocation pile-ups and microcracking at phase boundaries, but the specific mechanism of recrystallization reducing pile-ups is primarily evidenced by E3, with E1 and E2 providing only contextual support for the initial brittle behavior.
premises: Phase-selective recrystallization can fully recrystallize the soft FCC phase while retaining the hard B2/BCC skeleton in a eutectic HEA
Recrystallizing the soft phase eliminates weak boundaries and dislocation pile-up precursors, reducing local stress concentrations
Reducing dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries delays microcrack initiation and brittle failure
The preserved hard phase and its semi-coherent boundaries continue to block dislocations and promote work hardening
This treatment increases uniform tensile ductility (e.g., to ~35%) while maintaining or increasing strength (e.g., ~2 GPa true stress)
